part.text:
Now I understand the setup. The project page uses a single `Suspense` boundary that wraps both `getProjectTitle` and `getProjectDetails` (the slow one with 800ms delay). To make the title appear instantly while the rest loads, I need to:

1. Split the `Suspense` so the title resolves separately from the slow details.
2. Use `generateMetadata` for the title so it appears instantly in the document (and as a loading state).
3. Disable prefetching on the dashboard links.

Let me check the Next.js version for the right prefetch API.

Next.js 16. In Next 15+, `<Link prefetch={false}>` still works but the default already avoids prefetching the full data on the server (only the loading segment is prefetched by default). To explicitly avoid prefetching entirely, I'll set `prefetch={false}`.

part.text:
Build succeeds. The project page is now a Partial Prerender (◐) — the static shell (including the title via `generateMetadata`) is prerendered, while the slow details stream in.

Here's what I changed:

**`app/page.tsx`** — Added `prefetch={false}` to the dashboard links so navigating to a project doesn't prefetch the project page at all.

**`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`** — Two changes so the title appears instantly:
1. Added `generateMetadata` that calls only the fast `getProjectTitle`. Next.js streams the document `<title>` (and the prerendered static shell) immediately, before the slow details resolve.
2. Split the single `Suspense` boundary into two: one wrapping the title (fast) and one wrapping the details (the 800ms `getProjectDetails`). This lets the `<h1>` render as soon as its data is ready, independent of the slow details block, which shows a `Loading details...` fallback meanwhile.

Both `getProjectTitle` and `getProjectDetails` already use `'use cache'`, so the title is cached and returns instantly on repeat visits.
